messages:
Elle (Finance): FYI vendor sent invoice INV-2025-089 but the VAT number on it looks like it was only issued last month. Need to confirm their VAT reg effective date before we pay.
Matt (Sales): Customer said they're a UK-registered reseller and asked for a zero-rated invoice because it's B2B. I forwarded the vendor's VAT number earlier.
ACME Accounting: Hi — VAT reg effective date on our end is 2025-01-15. We included the VAT number on the invoice by mistake; happy to reissue if you need VAT charged instead.
Elle (Finance): Ok — if their effective date is 2025-01-15 and invoice date is 2025-01-10, that means the vendor wasn't registered when they invoiced us. We can't accept a VAT-free invoice retroactively. Can you reissue with VAT or provide a credit note + new invoice?
ACME Accounting: We can reissue. Will we need a credit note and new invoice or can you accept a corrected invoice?
Sofia (Tax): Quick checklist: 1) Confirm vendor's official VAT registration certificate (VRC) showing 2025-01-15. 2) If invoice date < reg date, vendor must reissue with VAT and show VAT on invoice. 3) If they want to credit and reissue, we need both documents for our records.
Elle (Finance): Please upload the VRC to the vendor record in Ramp and attach it here. Hold payment until we have the corrected invoice/credit note.
invoice-bot: Payment scheduled for INV-2025-089 on 2025-01-12 has been put on hold by finance. Reason: VAT validation pending.
Matt (Sales): tagging @ACME Accounting — can you push the reissued docs today? Customer is asking for quick turnaround. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ACME Accounting: Will send corrected invoice + credit note by EOD. Also, we ran a quick government VAT checker and the VAT number validates now.
Sofia (Tax): Once we have: VRC + credit note + reissued invoice, finance can process a corrected payment. Also log a note under vendor record: 'invoice dated before VAT reg — reissue obtained'.
Elle (Finance): Thanks — I'll close the hold after docs are attached. @Matt, please confirm customer ok with timing.
Matt (Sales): Confirmed with customer — fine to wait for corrected paperwork. :white_check_mark:
